PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Daniel 6:17: "A stone was brought, and laid on the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Darius the Mede

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Darius the Mede: early sixties; broad, settled build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and hair under a tall royal cap; lined, steady face with heavy brows. Signature outfit: a long purple court robe over a cream tunic, with a gold-embroidered collar and a deep blue sash. Signature prop: a signet ring of gold on his right hand.
- The den of lions: a deep circular stone pit cut into bare earth beside a royal enclosure, its walls of dressed grey limestone rising high above a sandy floor. A heavy wooden lid and an iron-banded gate sit at the rim, reached by a worn stone stair. Dry scrub and a few palms grow at the edge; no plants inside the pit.
- Only Darius the Mede, the den of lions have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Darius the Mede kneeling at the pit's edge, pressing his signet ring into sealing clay on the stone
Action: A heavy stone is being rolled over the den's opening as the king and his lords affix their seals to it
Setting: A stone-sealed pit in a Persian palace courtyard in Babylon, mud-brick and dressed stone walls
Secondary elements: Several Persian lords in court dress gathered close, one holding a lamp, attendants straining at the stone with ropes; Daniel is not shown
Mood: Solemn, tense and hushed, with a sense of irrevocable decision
Time of day: Night, clear and still, lit by torchlight and lamp glow
Composition: Eye-level view from the courtyard edge, the stone and kneeling king in the foreground, the lords arranged around the pit in the middle distance

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.

- Goliath: man of enormous height, over nine feet tall, broad-shouldered and heavily muscled, around forty years old. - Valley of Elah: a broad, shallow valley of the Judean lowlands between rounded hills of terraced limestone, with a dry watercourse winding through its floor. 1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Matthew 1:1: "The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: (none with fixed canon; show only figures the scene plan describes, or none)

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A stone bench bearing a rolled, closed scroll, set at the center of the courtyard
Action: Still moment; sunlight falls across the closed scroll as if the family line is being gathered and held
Setting: Stone village courtyard in Roman Judea beside a synagogue wall, fishing boats faintly visible in the distance
Secondary elements: Clay jars and a low stone wall; figures of Abraham and David stand quietly at the edges of the courtyard, unnamed by any written sign
Mood: Reverent, grounded and expectant
Time of day: Midday, bright daylight with clear dry warm air and light dust
Composition: Eye-level view across the courtyard, the scroll centered in the foreground with the two ancestral figures framing it on either side

ART STYLE: Ink & Watercolor
Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- After: Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):

Mood: Awe, reverence and quiet anticipation.

Materials and texture: Matte, chalky paint surface within the depicted world.
Composition: Balanced, legible staging with figures in a shallow space; the scene painted out to every edge and corner.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Simon Peter; Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord; The Twelve Disciples (collective)

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.
- The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.
- Sea of Galilee: a large freshwater lake set in hilly terrain of basalt and limestone, its shores sloping to pebbled and sandy beaches. 2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, John 11:43: "When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”"

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord; Lazarus of Bethany; Martha; Crowd in John

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.
- Lazarus of Bethany: man in his thirties; lean, medium build; olive skin weathered by sun; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard, streaked grey at the chin; calm, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown, with a dark wool cloak in earth-brown. Carries no props.
- Martha of Bethany: a woman in her thirties, of sturdy and capable build, with warm olive skin weathered by sun. Dark brown hair is covered by a plain linen head veil pulled back from a careful face with a firm mouth and tired, attentive eyes. Her signature outfit, worn most often, is an undyed ochre-brown tunic with a rust-red wool cloak over the shoulders, belted with a plain cord. She carries no signature props.
- Crowd in John: adults and some older children of Jewish and Gentile communities in Galilee and Judea, ages roughly 15 to 60; lean to sturdy build; olive to tan skin; dark or grey-streaked hair kept short or tied back, beards kept trimmed or unshaven among the men; plain, weathered faces showing the sun and labour. Signature outfit: a undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, earth brown or faded blue, with a long woollen cloak in dusty ochre, worn over the shoulders. Carries nothing alone.
- Only Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord, Lazarus of Bethany, Martha, Crowd in John have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

Primary subject: Jesus standing at the tomb entrance, arm raised toward the cave, face lifted in a commanding call
Action: Jesus calls out in a loud voice as Lazarus, still wrapped in burial linen, stirs at the back of the dark tomb
Setting: Rock-hewn tomb cave at the edge of Bethany with a rolled stone set aside at the entrance
Secondary elements: Martha kneeling or standing near the entrance with hands clasped, a crowd of mourners in plain tunics and cloaks gathered behind, a dim oil lamp glowing faintly inside the tomb
Mood: Awe, tense expectancy, reverent hope
Time of day: Late afternoon daylight, clear and still
Composition: Viewed from slightly inside the cave looking out, Jesus framed in the bright entrance with Lazarus in shadow behind, crowd spread across the foreground

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.

- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
- Image 2: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

- The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Jesus standing upright in the stern, one arm extended toward the water, calm and commanding.
Action: The wind ceases and the churning waves smooth as he speaks.
Setting: Open water of the Sea of Galilee at night, a fishing boat with a wooden stern, rocky shoreline and stone villages in the distance.
Secondary elements: Disciples crouched or clinging to the boat's sides and mast, soaked and startled, rain easing; a dim oil lamp in the boat; torn sail slackening.
Mood: Awe, relief and stunned reverence after terror.
Time of day: Night sky breaking toward pale dawn, storm clouds parting, air suddenly still.
Composition: Low viewpoint from within the boat, Jesus centered in the stern against the lightening sky, disciples framing the lower edges, sea stretching outward.

ART STYLE: Fresco
Rendering: A finished early Renaissance fresco-style painting of the work's world: calm, monumental figures, clear gestures and simple architecture, painted in soft matte color.
Negatives: Show the scene itself, never a wall, plaster cracks, painted border, frame or ornamental band. No letters or inscriptions anywhere, and halos, if any, are plain. Avoid photorealism and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Soft earth reds, ochres, sage greens and pale lapis blue on light grounds.
Lighting: Even, gentle daylight with soft modelling and few cast shadows.
Materials and texture: Matte, chalky paint surface within the depicted world.
Composition: Balanced, legible staging with figures in a shallow space; the scene painted out to every edge and corner.

- After: He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”

SCENE: one moment of The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, A Scandal in Bohemia, Part I ¶1: "To Sherlock Holmes she is always _the_ woman. I have seldom heard him mention her under any other name. In his eyes she eclipses and predominates the whole of her sex. It was not that he felt any emotion akin to love for Irene Adler. All emotions, and that one particularly, were abhorrent to his cold, precise but admirably balanced mind. He was, I take it, the most perfect reasoning and observing machine that the world has seen, but as a lover he would have placed himself in a false position. He never spoke of the softer passions, save with a gibe and a sneer. They were admirable things for the observer—excellent for drawing the veil from men’s motives and actions. But for the trained reasoner to admit such intrusions into his own delicate and finely adjusted temperament was to introduce a distracting factor which might throw a doubt upon all his mental results. Grit in a sensitive instrument, or a crack in one of his own high-power lenses, would not be more disturbing than a strong emotion in a nature such as his. And yet there was but one woman to him, and that woman was the late Irene Adler, of dubious and questionable memory."

SCENE: one moment of The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, A Scandal in Bohemia, Part I ¶1: "To Sherlock Holmes she is always _the_ woman. I have seldom heard him mention her under any other name. In his eyes she eclipses and predominates the whole of her sex. It was not that he felt any emotion akin to love for Irene Adler. All emotions, and that one particularly, were abhorrent to his cold, precise but admirably balanced mind. He was, I take it, the most perfect reasoning and observing machine that the world has seen, but as a lover he would have placed himself in a false position. He never spoke of the softer passions, save with a gibe and a sneer. They were admirable things for the observer—excellent for drawing the veil from men’s motives and actions. But for the trained reasoner to admit such intrusions into his own delicate and finely adjusted temperament was to introduce a distracting factor which might throw a doubt upon all his mental results. Grit in a sensitive instrument, or a crack in one of his own high-power lenses, would not be more disturbing than a strong emotion in a nature such as his. And yet there was but one woman to him, and that woman was the late Irene Adler, of dubious and questionable memory."
